subject.title: feat(mxc): add Windows MXC sandbox backend

question: After the registration-mode guard is fixed, should OpenClaw accept the `@microsoft/mxc-sdk`/`node-pty` native dependency graph and the upstream argv-carried `--config-base64` sandbox config boundary for this prerelease Windows sandbox plugin?
rationale: This choice involves native sandbox executables, a dependency install script, and sandbox policy visibility through process argv; automation can inspect the facts but cannot decide the security boundary for maintainers.

options.title: Accept After Guard
options.body: Fix the non-full registration side effect, then have a maintainer/secops owner approve the exact-head dependency graph and documented MXC SDK argv transport before merge.

options.title: Pause For Upstream Transport
options.body: Keep the PR open but defer merge until MXC SDK offers a non-argv config transport or stronger policy secrecy story.

options.title: Decline First-Party Package
options.body: Close or redirect the Windows MXC backend outside first-party OpenClaw packaging if maintainers do not want to own this sandbox dependency boundary.

recommendation.title: Accept After Guard
recommendation.body: Fix the non-full registration side effect, then have a maintainer/secops owner approve the exact-head dependency graph and documented MXC SDK argv transport before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They made the latest item-specific parity and acceptance request on this PR, so they are the best visible owner for the remaining merge decision.
